title: The 2 January 2026 unshielding
summary: Three withdrawals from a presumed exchange hot wallet in late December, then 276,077.739 ZEC leaving the shielded pool in a single afternoon, of which 26.8 percent reached the exchange wallet and 73.2 percent has not moved since.

steps.note: Withdrawal from the hot wallet to a freshly created address. Input 120,552.69 ZEC in, 29,999.99 out, 90,552.70 change back to itself: textbook exchange-withdrawal mechanics.
Second withdrawal to the same address. Not separately reported in the press.
Third withdrawal, bringing the total to 49,999.97 ZEC. The press reported only the first 30,000.
The single largest unshielding of the period, from a transaction with zero transparent inputs. It did not go to an exchange: the address has never spent and still holds exactly this balance.
The fresh address spends all four of its UTXOs into a transaction with zero transparent outputs, shielding its entire balance, and never appears again.
Fifty-two minutes later, a transaction with zero transparent inputs creates a single output 0.4059 ZEC smaller. The alignment is four-fold and the link is unprovable by design.
Second unshielding tranche. Its origin inside the pool is unknown.
Both tranches consolidated and sent to the hot wallet. The press reported 74,002 ZEC and dated it 3 or 5 January; on-chain it is the 2nd.
A classic many-to-one deposit sweep, which supports the hot-wallet reading independently of any third-party label.

verdict: 276,077.739 ZEC left the shielded pool on 2 January 2026, about 1.63 percent of the then-circulating supply and higher than the figure the press reported, which counted only the largest tranche. 74,001.93 ZEC reached a major exchange hot wallet. Roughly 50,000 of that plausibly originated from the same wallet eight days earlier, which would make the widely-reported whale deposit at most about 24,000 ZEC of genuinely new inflow. Zcash's design means the shield and the unshield cannot be proven to be the same coins, and nothing here establishes who owns any address or that anything was sold.

title: The ZIP 271 lockbox: near-total inaction, then untraceability
summary: The entire deferred dev-fund lockbox was disbursed in one coinbase transaction to a consensus-defined multisig. Twenty months later 99.28 percent of it has never moved, and everything that did move went straight into the shielded pool, as the ZIP requires.

steps.from: protocol lockbox value pool (NU6.1 activation coinbase)
steps.note: Ten outputs of 7,875 ZEC to the 2-of-3 multisig named in the ZIP 271 consensus rules.
The first and only chunk ever spent, shielded as ZIP 271 mandates. Blockchair mislabels the whole amount as a fee; it is not a fee, it is shielded value.
94.5 percent of the chunk returns to the multisig twenty minutes later. Net out of that operation: 436.7705 ZEC.
A second, much smaller shielded disbursement.

verdict: Fact: 78,183.4093 ZEC, 99.28 percent of the lockbox, is still sitting in the multisig, with nine of ten chunks completely untouched. Fact: the 566.5907 ZEC that has moved went into shielded outputs. Inference, medium: the amounts retained are consistent with grant disbursements under ZIP 1016. Not knowable: whether any recipient sold. ZIP 271 requires each chunk to be spent completely into a shielded output, so the trail terminates at the first hop by design, not by any failure of research.

title: The 202,076 ZEC unshielding that never moved
summary: The largest single exit from the shielded pool in the period went to an address that had been tested with one ZEC nine days earlier and has not spent a zatoshi since.

steps.note: A one ZEC test deposit, nine days before the address received two hundred thousand.
A transaction with zero transparent inputs. As of 2026-08-22 the balance is unchanged and the address has never spent.

verdict: Proves that a single entity moved roughly 165 million dollars of ZEC out of shielding and has held it transparently ever since. Proves it did not go to an exchange. Does not prove who owns it, or why. An aggregator dated a 202,077 ZEC move to 2025-12-20 and called it a Binance withdrawal; no address was published, and the only on-chain event of that size is this one, thirteen days later in the wrong direction. Treat the aggregator's date and direction as unconfirmed.
